provenance.url: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/data/FPCPITOTLZGDEU (World Bank World Development Indicators, 'Inflation, consumer prices for Germany'); cross-checked against https://www.officialdata.org/germany/inflation and https://www.destatis.de/EN/Press/2026/01/PE26_019_611.html
provenance.license: World Bank WDI data is freely redistributable; Destatis (German Federal Statistical Office) press releases are public-domain government statistics.
provenance.note: Built backward from 2025=100 using year-over-year % change in annual-average German CPI (World Bank WDI series FPCPITOTLZGDEU), same construction method as us.json's cpiIndex (index[y] = index[y+1]/(1+inflation[y+1])). All years 1980-2025 are official annual inflation-rate observations, none interpolated. CURRENCY NOTE: this is a price-LEVEL index (base 2025=100), which is currency-agnostic because it is built purely by chaining annual inflation percentages. Years 1980-1998 are in 'DM-equivalent price level terms' (West Germany used the Deutsche Mark until the Euro became the official accounting currency on 1999-01-01 and physical cash on 2002-01-01); these index values are NOT directly convertible into EUR amounts year-by-year (i.e. do not divide a 1990 DM price by the index to get a EUR price) — they only represent how much *general price levels* rose or fell, which composes correctly across the DM->EUR redenomination. From 1999 onward the index values correspond to EUR-era inflation.

provenance.url: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/data/ECBDFR (ECB Deposit Facility Rate for Euro Area); rate-change dates cross-checked against https://www.ecb.europa.eu/pub/pdf/annrep/ecb.ar_annex2020_statistical_section~ae79ac8ab8.en.pdf and Bundesbank 'Long time series on economic development in Germany' (https://www.bundesbank.de/resource/blob/844802/.../i-3-geld-und-kapitalmarkt-data.pdf)
provenance.license: Public domain / central bank statistics (ECB, redistributed via FRED; Bundesbank publications).
provenance.note: EUR-ERA ONLY (1999-2025): the ECB Deposit Facility Rate (the rate German/Euro-area banks earn on overnight deposits with the Eurosystem) is used as a proxy for a German/Euro-area risk-free savings return, in the same spirit as us.json's use of the 1-Year T-bill rate as a stand-in for a 'savings' return. Annual figures are time-weighted averages of the rate across all rate-change dates within each calendar year (computed from the daily ECBDFR series), NOT simple year-end snapshots. ESTIMATED/approximate for all years: although the underlying rate-change dates and levels are official ECB decisions, the day-count weighting used to produce an annual average was computed manually from known decision dates rather than sourced as a pre-published annual-average series, so treat these as a secondary/estimated derivation. Negative values (2014-2021) reflect the ECB's negative interest rate policy era; actual German retail savings accounts were typically floored near 0% during this period rather than charging savers negative rates, so realized retail experience was likely somewhat better than this series for those years. No data before 1999 because Germany used the Deutsche Mark (DM) until the Euro became official accounting currency in 1999 and physical cash in 2002; mixing DM-era Bundesbank rates with EUR-era ECB rates into one 'return' series would conflate different currencies, so this series intentionally starts in 1999.

provenance.license: Index levels are public historical market data; DAX is a Deutsche Boerse / Qontigo (STOXX) product; aggregator sites (Wikipedia, wallstreetnumbers.com, topforeignstocks.com, 1stock1.com, finanzen.net) republish historical closing levels.
provenance.note: EUR-ERA ONLY (1999-2025): DAX is Germany's blue-chip total-return (performance) index, meaning dividends are reinvested into the index level (unlike the price-only S&P 500 series used in us.json). Year-end (last trading day of year) DAX closes, 1999-2025. Years 1999-2024 are corroborated across 2+ independent sources (Wikipedia 'DAX' annual-returns table, wallstreetnumbers.com, topforeignstocks.com, 1stock1.com, and finanzen.net's Jahresende figures for 2020/2021/2023) and match well-known public DAX annual-return figures (e.g. -43.9% in 2002, -40.4% in 2008, -18.3% in 2018, -12.3% in 2022, +20.3% in 2023, +18.8% in 2024). The 2025 close (24488.24, implying an approx. +23% annual return) is an ESTIMATE based on a single source (m.ticker.com) reporting a rounded 2025 year-end value/return and has not been independently corroborated — treat 2025 de_stock figures as the least certain in this series. No DAX/EUR data before 1999 is included here because the DAX was DM-denominated before 1999; mixing DM-denominated and EUR-denominated index levels into one return/closes series would conflate currencies, so this series intentionally starts in 1999 (EUR era).
